comment.narrative: Limited capacity to identify hotspot areas and root causes of electoral violence for the 8th of August 2017 Elections
hot spot areas are accurately identified to prevent and mitigate electoral violence

The identification and mitigation of hotspot areas for the prevention of electoral violence have been executed with precision. A comprehensive conflict mapping and analysis grounded in the principles outlined in the Early Warning and Early Response EPEAESTA papers was disseminated to the National Cohesion and Integration Commission NCIC Commission. This information played a pivotal role in shaping the projects priority activities leading up to the election aligning seamlessly with NCICs priorities as outlined in the revised Work Plan of June 2022.This network played an important role in conflict resolution by providing valuable information to the National Cohesion and Integration Commission NCIC and other stakeholders. Weekly monthly and thematic reports were consistently generated and shared totaling 11 monthly reports and 49 weekly reports.Furthermore the successful integration of the Media Monitoring and Early Warning situation room software ensured its full functionality.The Election Situation Room operated throughout the election cycle facilitating efficient collaboration between the NCIC Early Warning mechanism and the Media Monitoring Unit. This integration streamlined the reporting process allowing reports from Cohesion Monitors at the county level to converge efficiently into the Situation Room through Regional Coordinators.

comment.narrative: No activities implemented before the start of intervention

Our intervention in response to the challenges arising from the 2017 elections has been instrumental in cultivating tolerance trust and coexistence among Kenyan communities. In light of the evolving priorities of the National Cohesion and Integration Commission NCIC our project strategically adapted placing a more significant emphasis on community dialogues as a central strategy to address intercommunity violence and emerging crises.This adaptive approach resulted in tangible advancements notably evidenced in improved mutual understanding and trust among local communities as underscored in both the BTOR and endofmission reports. The NCIC postelection report explicitly recognises the efficacy of our project in facilitating communityled initiatives and grassroots reconciliation efforts. These endeavours significantly contributed to advancing peace and fostering enhanced intra and intercommunal relations aligning with the core objectives of our intervention in the electoral landscape.

description.narrative: Functioning election violence mitigating mechanisms (national programme)

comment.narrative: The project has effectively established robust mechanisms for mitigating election violence on a national scale. Employing EURECS cuttingedge methodologies specifically the Economic Political Economy Analyses EPEA and Election Security Threat Assessment ESTA our program operates proactively to map and monitor potential electoral threats considering the intricate dynamics of political and economic processes. The regular reports generated by ESTA provide realtime insights into emerging conflicts enabling timely interventions. Additionally the systematic approach of EPEA allows for a comprehensive understanding of the broader electoral landscape. Through the strategic use of these tools the project ensures alignment with European Union EU indicators placing a strong emphasis on transparency and resilience in electoral processes. This substantiates the projects success in creating functioning mechanisms for the mitigation of election violence on a national level.

comment.narrative: 2017 Elections marred with violence around election. Challenges in the management of sensitivities
target of no violence and peaceful acceptance of results and Improved understanding tolerance trust and peaceful coexistence among Kenyans

The 2022 Kenyan elections witnessed opposition from four IEBC commissioners who disowned the results due to transparency concerns. Legal challenges centred on a small number of issues and undisclosed results leading to nine petitions.On September 5 the Supreme Court unanimously dismissed the petitions affirming the elections validity. The court addressed issues such as technology standards form uploads alleged discrepancies and constitutional processes.Postelection Presidentelect Ruto secured a majority while the opposition accepted the courts ruling. The transition to Rutos presidency was relatively calm with minimal protests and isolated incidents. This underscores the pivotal role of legal frameworks in addressing challenges during and after the elections.

Extensive pool of electoral officials and stakeholders with enhanced understanding regarding the medias role in electoral conflict prevention

ECES and NCIC collaboratively executed an extensive media campaign aimed at fostering peace throughout the nation. This initiative was complemented by the strategic training of 30 journalists 16 male 14 female in conflictsensitive reporting. The objective was to enhance journalists skills empower them to devise strategies for promoting peaceful coexistence discourage propaganda and polarisation and uphold professionalism in reporting. The comprehensive training covered diverse topics including the legal framework governing media freedom of expression and hate speech in Kenya as well as the roles and responsibilities of journalists during electoral processes. Furthermore sessions on ethical rules international standards disinformation and factchecking equipped journalists with additional skills crucial for ethical reporting.In conjunction with the training a series of impactful interventions were implemented including 13 townhall forums in eight regions 40 primetime peace messages in the form of short clips and four interviews featuring representatives from ECES and NCIC discussing peacebuilding and conflict mitigation. The incorporation of disruptive elements such as SqueezeBacks Popups and Lower Thirds strategically designed to capture audience attention further amplified the reach of peace messages. Notably 30 journalists who underwent the training actively contributed to the improvement in election reporting by adopting conflictsensitive approaches ethical standards and effective verification techniques.The multifaceted approach combining training with targeted media interventions has made substantial strides in addressing the perception of media reporting on elections in a conflict and gendersensitive manner. The undertaken initiatives have undeniably contributed to a more nuanced ethical and responsible reporting landscape thereby partially meeting the goal of promoting conflict and gendersensitive election reporting.

1EPEAESTA Report 1 Media Monitoring report and 1 Early WarningThe creation of three EPEAESTA reports is central to our projects commitment to developing crucial learning tools on reconciliation mediation conflict management conflict transformation and stabilization. These reports meticulously document the projects journey. On one hand EPEA is a systematic approach using the EPEA methodology to monitor diverse processes delving into the interaction of political and economic processes and exploring power and wealth distribution. It helps understand the driving forces behind political behavior and their impact on policy development. On the other hand ESTA a copyrighted stakeholder mapping activity proactively prevents electoral conflicts. Developed by ECES it operates in conjunction with other methodologies including EPEA LEAD and PEV. ESTA continually maps security threats engaging with the security sector to understand and mitigate potential risks. Our additional efforts such as daily media digests weekly Media Monitoring reports and weekly Early Warning reports demonstrate our commitment to providing timely insights. The Early Warning teams contributions with 49 weekly reports and 11 monthly reports substantially enhance our documentation facilitating a robust impact assessment.

comment.narrative: 10 Dialogue meetings with 25 participants are held and peace charters signed by key actors in all identified hotspot areas.

The ProPeace Kenya project engaged in 11 impactful intra and intercommunal dialogues across diverse regions significantly contributing to conflict resolution and the strengthening of peace infrastructure. In Isiolo County pivotal dialogues held in Mulango and Kipsing targeted six distinct communities fostering understanding and cooperation to alleviate tensions. Samburu County witnessed a comprehensive series of dialogues in Laresoro Sereolipi and Lengusaka engaging 216 participants and empowering communities in proactive peacebuilding. Crucial stakeholder engagements in Marsabit County addressed potential conflicts and fostered peaceful coexistence among historically conflicting communities. Structured dialogues in Laikipia County conducted from February 2 to February 11 2023 involving 152 participants focused on persistent landrelated conflicts resulting in resolutions that promoted cohesion and harmony. The Garissa County Interclan Peace Agreements Dialogue Forum held from August 22 to August 24 2023 engaged stakeholders in addressing escalating violence covering crucial issues such as clan tensions land grabbing and the role of social media in fueling tensions. In the Kerio Valley Region a Political Leaders Meeting in Machakos County on April 25 2023 involved leaders from West Pokot Baringo Turkana and Elgeyo Marakwet Counties focusing on actionable peacebuilding strategies. Additionally a Professional Meeting in Nakuru County on March 29th and 30th 2023 gathered professionals from various sectors to address challenges in the region contributing to a ceasefire peaceoriented activities and collaborative efforts for sustainable peace. As part of evolving objectives plans for Mediation and Reconciliation Roundtables transformed into three distinct events the Wajibika Regional Youth Dialogue Conference and two Kerio Valley Cluster Political Meetings. This adaptive approach aligned seamlessly with the projects commitment to effectively resolve conflicts and curb electoralrelated violence showcasing a dynamic and comprehensive approach to fostering lasting peace.

comment.narrative: Communications campaign to promote peace and inclusion in electoral processes are developed. The resulting messages will be aired on the radio 5 daily snippets for 2 months prior to the elections and spread through posters in public areas 200 in each of the 47 counties.

The projects media campaign designed to promote peace and unity for violencefree elections strategically disseminated peace messages to diverse stakeholders. The integrated media strategy ensured information reached political party youth wings womens organisations and the public fostering awareness.One of its central initiatives was the production of the national peace song One Kenya One People One Love featuring prominent artists. The songs dissemination across traditional and mainstream media garnered significant interest reaching millions of Kenyans and accumulating about 500000 hits on YouTube.To address highrisk counties two peace caravans were deployed in Uasin Gishu and Nakuru reaching approximately 5000 individuals. Notably Nakuru historically significant for the 2012 Nakuru County Peace Accord played a crucial role in promoting national coexistence.MimiMkenya town hall forums conducted in Kisumu and Kericho in collaboration with NTV aimed at fostering unity and peaceful coexistence. Utilising various channels including print articles radio interviews and digital media the forums targeted 1200 participants and reached a total of 3154000 people.The projects pinnacle was the Peace Concert at Nakuru Athletics Club attended by key figures such as the NMG leadership the EU Ambassador the Governor of Nakuru County and the Chairman of NCIC. The event aimed at bolstering patriotism strengthening peace efforts and encouraging constructive electoral conversations.The media campaigns success can be attributed to its strategic multifaceted approach which incorporates town hall meetings peace caravans concerts and the impactful Only Love song. These efforts collectively contributed to achieving the projects outcome of fostering peace cohesion and ensuring peaceful elections.

comment.narrative: According to the KNCHR 37 people were killed. The EU EOM Report noted violence across the electoral processes and in the post electoral period.

In the aftermath of the 2022 presidential elections in Kenya the postelection environment maintained relative calm with the majority of areas experiencing peaceful transitions. However its essential to note two incidents of burned houses in Uasin Gishu county immediately following the elections. These isolated acts of violence interpreted by the affected community as a warning contribute to shaping the public perception of the overall security situation during the postelection period.Despite these incidents the broader postelection landscape remained relatively stable. Following the formal gazetting of Ruto as the presidentelect and the rejection of the election outcome by Odinga there were limited spontaneous protests with some car destruction in Kisumu and Nairobi. The police responded with proportionality and restraint successfully quelling the protests and maintaining order. Overall while these isolated incidents of violence occurred they represent exceptions in an environment that for the most part saw a controlled and calm transition after the presidential elections.

In the framework of our programme this paramount indicator has been the tangible evidence of reduced incidences of political and electoralrelated violence. This aligns seamlessly with the EUs focus on tracking the number of violent incidents in targeted action areas. With our activities rooted in the principles of mediation conflict prevention and resilience weve actively conducted mass and targeted awareness campaigns and advocated for legislative changes such as the 2022 amendment to the Political Parties Act. Our sustained collaboration with the IEBC and the ORPP has bolstered the enforcement of the Electoral Code of Conduct leading to a tangible decrease in violent incidents. This outcome not only validates the effectiveness of our programmes strategies but also corresponds directly with EU indicators showcasing our commitment to international standards of peaceful electoral conduct.
